title: Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection on quit when CharacterBody2D overlaps Area2D
body:
### Tested versions

Tested in Godot 4.7

### System information

Running Linux 7.0.13-1-MANJARO kernel, Godot Engine v4.7.stable.official.5b4e0cb0f, Vulkan 1.4.341 - Forward+,  NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5050 Laptop GPU

### Issue description

Disconnection of signals within the scene tree does not complete gracefully on quit where a CharacterBody2D overlaps an Area2D.  

The following type of error occurs:
```
ERROR: Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection from 'CharacterBody2D:<CharacterBody2D#31977375089>'. Signal: 'tree_entered', callable: ''.
   at: _disconnect (core/object/object.cpp:1643)
ERROR: Attempt to disconnect a nonexistent connection from 'CharacterBody2D:<CharacterBody2D#31977375089>'. Signal: 'tree_exiting', callable: ''.
   at: _disconnect (core/object/object.cpp:1643)
```


### Steps to reproduce

The included reproduction project has:

- A 2D scene
- An Area2D with a CollisionShape2D to define its collision area
- A CharacterBody2D with a CollisionShape2D to define its collision area
- An autoload to quit the project with the following code:

```
extends Node

func _unhandled_input(event):
	if event is InputEventKey:
		if event.pressed and event.keycode == KEY_ESCAPE:
			get_tree().quit.call_deferred()
```


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29538878/test.zip)
